items.hint: Find the acute angle between the terminal side and the $x$-axis first, then decide whether the $x$-coordinate is positive or negative in that quadrant.
worked: The terminal side of $\dfrac{5\pi}{6}$ lies in quadrant II.
Cosine is the $x$-coordinate, and $x$ is negative in quadrant II, so $\cos\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right)=-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.

items.stem: A student evaluates $\sin\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{6}\right)$ and writes: the terminal side is in quadrant III, the reference angle is $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$, and $\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)=\dfrac{1}{2}$, so $\sin\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{6}\right)=\dfrac{1}{2}$. Which statement identifies what went wrong?
items.hint: Her reference angle is fine, so check the sign of the $y$-coordinate at a point in quadrant III.
worked: Reference angle: $\dfrac{7\pi}{6}-\pi=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$, so the size of the answer really is $\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)=\dfrac{1}{2}$.
In quadrant III both coordinates are negative, and sine is the $y$-coordinate.
The reference angle sets the size and the quadrant sets the sign, so $\sin\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{6}\right)=-\dfrac{1}{2}$.

options.text: The reference angle is right, but sine is the $x$-coordinate, so the value is $-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.
The reference angle is right, but sine is negative in quadrant III, so the value is $-\dfrac{1}{2}$.

items.stem: Find every angle $\theta$ in $[0,2\pi)$ for which $\tan\theta=-\sqrt{3}$.
items.hint: Get the acute angle whose tangent is $\sqrt{3}$ first, then ask in which two quadrants tangent comes out negative.
worked: Size first: $\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=\sqrt{3}$, so the reference angle is $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$.
Sign next: $\tan\theta=\dfrac{y}{x}$ is negative where $x$ and $y$ have opposite signs, which is quadrants II and IV.
Quadrant II gives $\pi-\dfrac{\pi}{3}=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$; quadrant IV gives $2\pi-\dfrac{\pi}{3}=\dfrac{5\pi}{3}$.
